tier_justification: The pinning contract (no move, and the drop guarantee) and its purpose (self-references, intrusive collections) are documented informally in core::pin and in Jung's 2018 posts; here the implication from the contract to two concrete address-sensitive invariants is made precise and mechanized for a toy heap.
plain_claim: For every list acts of primitive actions run from the empty toy heap State.init (every list of Act is allowed): if no action moves a value out of a pinned field location holding a non-Unpin value (Always NoPinnedMove State.init acts) and no action deallocates or overwrites the memory of such a value before its destructor has run (Always DropGuaranteeAct State.init acts), then in every visited state every set self-pointer points at its own field location (SelfRefOK) and every intrusive-list entry finds, at its address, the value that registered (ListOK).

hypotheses.name: hmove : Always NoPinnedMove State.init acts
hypotheses.purpose: No action moves a value out of a pinned field location whose value is not Unpin (compiler moves, such as packed drop glue, count as moves).
hypotheses.witness_class: a one-object, one-field trace of 5 primitive actions from State.init (coreMoveActs)

hypotheses.name: hdrop : Always DropGuaranteeAct State.init acts
hypotheses.purpose: The drop guarantee: no deallocation or overwrite of a pinned non-Unpin value's memory before its destructor runs.
hypotheses.witness_class: a one-object, one-field trace of 6 primitive actions from State.init (coreReuseActs)

nonvacuity_witness: coreNonVacuousActs: 21 actions that pin a non-Unpin value, set its self-pointer, link it into the list, move a pinned Unpin value and an unpinned non-Unpin value, swap, drop in place, write into emptied locations, deallocate and leak; both hypotheses hold and the self-pointer and list entry are really established.
non_claims: These are statements about the toy model (model–system relation: none proved); they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about Rust's Pin API, the Rust standard library or the Rust compiler. Actions, invariants and states are a toy; the readings 'NoPinnedMove = no &mut to a pinned non-Unpin value is used to move it' and 'DropGuaranteeAct = the documented drop guarantee' are modeling bridges (derived), not theorems.

The informal form 'no &mut to a pinned non-Unpin value is ever produced' is not the hypothesis. On one 6-operation program, producing a non-structural &mut and using it only to assign in place (drop, then write) keeps both invariants (projection_inconsistent_assign_harmless); no general statement about move-free uses of &mut is proved here.

hmove and hdrop are tight for this universally quantified theorem, with one-object, one-field witness traces (noPinnedMove_tight, dropGuarantee_tight); in particular 'no moves' alone does not suffice (dropGuarantee_tight). They are not necessary on an individual trace: moving a pinned non-Unpin value that never stored its address or linked itself, or overwriting one that only set a self-pointer, keeps AddrInv on that trace (noPinnedMove_not_necessary_on_a_trace, dropGuaranteeAct_not_necessary_on_a_trace).

'Pinned' means that pinField has run on that field location. Pinning an object (Act.pinObj) by itself protects none of its fields under NoPinnedMove or DropGuaranteeAct, and pinField protects a field even if the object was never pinned (pinObj_inert_in_core, pinField_without_pinObj_protects); SafeOp, not the primitive actions, requires the object to be pinned before a structural projection.

Built-in modeling assumption, not a hypothesis: self-pointers and list entries are established only at a pinned field location holding a non-Unpin value (setSelf and register are no-ops otherwise). Types that rely on their address while being Unpin, or that set up such reliance before being pinned, are outside the model.

Two address-sensitive invariants are modelled: a field location's value pointing to that same location, and one external list holding field locations. Pointers from one field to a sibling field of the same struct (as in compiler-generated async state machines), pointers between distinct values, interior pointers and pointer arithmetic are not modelled.

dropTemp and freeTemp act on the most recently allocated object whatever its origin (address heap.length - 1 with truncated subtraction; on the empty heap both are no-ops, tempActs_noop_on_empty_heap); on a heap whose last object is a pinned non-Unpin value, freeTemp is excluded by hdrop (dropGuaranteeAct_neg).
Starts from the empty heap; no claim for arbitrary initial states.
No claim about undefined behaviour under any Rust aliasing model: 'invariant broken' means a stale pointer exists in the toy state.

design_question: Which action-level discipline keeps self-pointers and intrusive-list entries of pinned values valid, and does dropping either part of the pinning contract (no moves; the drop guarantee) admit a trace that breaks them?

tier_justification: The four requirements of core::pin (structural Unpin, pinned destruction including not packed, drop guarantee, no move-out operations) plus the documented consistency of the projection choice, made precise for a toy struct and mechanized; pin-project enforces the same list.
plain_claim: For every toy struct declaration d: if (a) d is declared Unpin (d.unpin = true) only when every structurally projected field (ApiOp.projPin i in d.api) has an Unpin type, (b) its destructor does not move out of a structurally projected field of non-Unpin type, (c) neither its API nor its destructor overwrites such a field without dropping its value, (d) it offers no Pin<&mut S> -> F move-out of such a field, (e) it is not packed when it has such a field, and (f) such a field is not also offered through a non-structural projection, then every program accepted by SafeProgram d from State.init (a list of Op, compiled to primitive actions by compile d) keeps SelfRefOK and ListOK in every visited state.

hypotheses.name: ha : UnpinOnlyIfPinnedFieldsUnpin d
hypotheses.purpose: (a) declared Unpin only if every structurally projected field's type is Unpin; otherwise Pin::get_mut yields &mut S and mem::replace moves the pinned field.
hypotheses.witness_class: a one-field declaration (dA) and a 5-operation safe program

hypotheses.name: hb : DtorNoMoveOutOfPinned d
hypotheses.purpose: (b) The destructor (which receives &mut self) does not move out of a structurally projected non-Unpin field.
hypotheses.witness_class: a one-field declaration (dB) and a 5-operation safe program

hypotheses.name: hc : DropGuaranteeForPinned d
hypotheses.purpose: (c) Neither the API nor the destructor overwrites a structurally projected non-Unpin field without dropping its value. Both conjuncts are tight separately.
hypotheses.witness_class: one-field declarations (dC: API overwrite; dC': destructor overwrite) and 5-operation safe programs

hypotheses.name: hd : NoPinnedTake d
hypotheses.purpose: (d) No Pin<&mut S> -> F move-out (Option::take-like) for a structurally projected non-Unpin field.
hypotheses.witness_class: a one-field declaration (dD) and a 5-operation safe program

hypotheses.name: he : NotPackedIfPinned d
hypotheses.purpose: (e) Not #[repr(packed)] when there is a structurally projected non-Unpin field (packed drop glue moves fields to aligned temporaries).
hypotheses.witness_class: a one-field declaration (dE) and a 5-operation safe program

hypotheses.name: hf : ProjectionConsistent d
hypotheses.purpose: (f) A structurally projected non-Unpin field is not also offered through a non-structural projection Pin<&mut S> -> &mut F.
hypotheses.witness_class: a one-field declaration (dF) and a 6-operation safe program

hypotheses.name: hsafe : SafeProgram d State.init prog
hypotheses.purpose: Restricts to programs every operation of which SafeOp permits in the state where it runs (e.g. a &mut to a field or to S only when SafeOp provides one).
hypotheses.witness_class: the one-field declaration dBase (satisfying (a)-(f)) and the 5-operation program progA

nonvacuity_witness: dRich: three fields (non-Unpin structurally projected; non-Unpin non-structural with take, overwrite and a destructor that moves it out and overwrites it; Unpin with both projections); progRich: 20 safe operations including pinning, a self-reference, two list entries, replace/swap/take/overwrite/assign of non-structural fields, replacing an unpinned struct, leaking, and dropping. All six conditions and safety hold; the conclusion is also checked directly (structural_nonvacuous_conclusion).
non_claims: (a)-(e) alone are not sufficient in this model (conditions_a_to_e_insufficient): for the one-field declaration dF a non-structural &mut to the structurally projected field lets mem::swap move it.

The conditions constrain only structurally projected fields whose type is not Unpin; for Unpin fields they hold vacuously (conditions_vacuous_without_pinned_nonUnpin). For a generic field type T, a library must meet them for non-Unpin instantiations, which gives the documentation's unqualified requirements; this generic reading is a modeling bridge, not proved.

'Structurally pinned field' means exactly ApiOp.projPin i in d.api. Self-pointers and list entries arise only at such fields (addrState_only_at_structurally_projected_fields). Private fields whose address S's own unsafe code relies on without offering a structural projection, and pointers between sibling fields, are outside the model.

Field alignment is not modelled: dPermissive is packed, has a structurally projected field of Unpin type and satisfies (a)-(f), whereas in Rust taking a reference to a possibly unaligned field of a #[repr(packed)] struct is rejected or undefined behaviour and core::pin says pinning cannot be used with packed types (pin.rs lines 630-633) (modeling bridge).
Soundness for Unpin fields relies on the built-in modeling assumption that Unpin values never establish self-pointers or list entries (Act.setSelf and Act.register are no-ops on them).

The safe API is closed: safe code can do exactly the Op constructors; S's own operations are the four ApiOp forms (take and overwrite are callable whether or not the object is pinned, which only adds programs) and its destructor is a list of the two DtorOp forms (move a field out; overwrite a field without drop). Destructors that drop a field in place and then reuse its storage, and arbitrary unsafe-implemented APIs (e.g. RefCell-like get_pin_mut plus borrow_mut), are covered insofar as they reduce to these forms and are not covered otherwise.
After Op.forget b, references to b stay usable in this model (closer to Box::leak than to mem::forget); see forget-frame-and-leaked-object-never-dropped-by-safe-continuations.

One struct type, one level of fields (no nested structural pinning), a field is either empty or occupied (no general enums), no shared pinning (Pin<&S>), no interior mutability, no panics or unwinding, no concurrency.
Values moved out by replaceField/take are dropped immediately; packed drop glue is modelled as moving every field to a fresh temporary; which fields a real compiler moves is not examined.
Not a soundness proof for pin-project, the standard library, or any crate.

design_question: Which conditions on a struct's declaration (Unpin, destructor, API, packedness, projection choice) make structural projection Pin<&mut S> -> Pin<&mut F> sound for every safe program?

tier_justification: Each failure mode is described informally in core::pin (the Option::take example, the packed-drop remark, the RefCell example); here each is a concrete, checked program in the toy model.
plain_claim: For each of (a)-(f) there is a one-field toy declaration that satisfies the other five conditions and violates that one, together with a program of at most six operations accepted by SafeProgram from State.init along which AddrInv fails: for (a), (b), (d), (e), (f) the program sets a self-pointer, SelfRefOK fails in some visited state and ListOK holds in all of them; for (c), both by S's API (dC) and by its destructor (dC'), the program links into the list, ListOK fails in some visited state and SelfRefOK holds in all of them. Replacing the self-pointer by a list link in the (a), (b), (d), (e), (f) programs gives programs accepted by SafeProgram along which ListOK fails; with a self-pointer only, the (c) overwrite keeps AddrInv.
nonvacuity_witness: Not applicable (closed statements without hypotheses); each theorem exhibits its declaration (dA, dB, dC, dC', dD, dE, dF) and program and checks every conjunct by evaluation.
non_claims: These theorems establish tightness of (a)-(f) in addrInv_of_structural_pinning_conditions within the class of one-field declarations and programs of at most six operations; they do not prove the universal converses (for every d, SafeProgramsKeepAddrInv d implies the condition) (not proved here), and they do not enumerate all exploitations.

Condition (c) is invisible to the self-reference invariant on its witness: with only a self-reference the same overwrite keeps both invariants (dropGuaranteeForPinned_invisible_to_selfRef). A model with only self-referential values would make (c) look unneeded.

Escape hatches that defeat the witnesses: if the projected field's type is Unpin, or ApiOp.projPin i is not offered, all six conditions hold vacuously (conditions_vacuous_without_pinned_nonUnpin and the definition of Decl.PinnedNonUnpinField); if the object is leaked instead of dropped, the destructor-triggered failures (b), (c)-destructor and (e) do not occur on it (leaked_object_never_dropped_or_deallocated).
'Breaks an invariant' means a stale pointer in the toy state; no claim that the corresponding Rust program has undefined behaviour under a particular aliasing model.
The packed witness models the compiler moving the field before dropping it; whether a particular compiler version moves a particular (aligned) field is not examined.

non_claims: Scope boundary: in this model a location is a field location (b, i); no location denotes a whole struct, so the struct itself never holds a self-pointer or list entry, and every self-pointer target and list entry created by a safe program lies at a field index with an offered structural projection (addrState_only_at_structurally_projected_fields). A declaration with no structural projection therefore satisfies PinnedFieldsUnpin vacuously and keeps AddrInv for every safe program whatever its unpin value, because it never has any address-sensitive state (sound_of_pinnedFieldsUnpin, no_addrState_without_structural_projection; instance noProjection_unpin_vacuously_sound).

Do not apply this to conclude that a Rust type that is itself address-sensitive may implement Unpin, for example a self-referential leaf type with no projecting methods, or a #[pin_project] struct whose PhantomPinned marker lacks #[pin] (pin-project documents that PhantomPinned without #[pin] has no effect, lib.rs lines 297-313). Such types are outside the model; for them Unpin must be suppressed (modeling bridge).

A declared-Unpin struct may not offer a structural projection of a non-Unpin field, whatever the other conditions: unpinWitness_breaks_selfRef_of_unpin_of_structural_nonUnpin_field gives a breaking safe program for every such declaration.

hypotheses.name: hu : d.unpin = true
hypotheses.purpose: Declaring S : Unpin is what makes &mut S, hence the whole-struct replace, available to safe code on a pinned S.
hypotheses.witness_class: the one-field declaration dBase with i = 0

hypotheses.name: hproj : ApiOp.projPin i ∈ d.api
hypotheses.purpose: Field i is structurally projected, so the program can pin it and let it store its address.
hypotheses.witness_class: the one-field declaration dUnpinNonStructural with i = 0

hypotheses.name: hty : d.fieldTy i = false

tier_justification: The documentation and Jung's post state that leaking (mem::forget of a Box) satisfies the drop guarantee because the storage is never freed or reused; made precise for the toy model.
plain_claim: (1) For every toy state st and address b: Act.forget b changes no leaf, pinned location, pinned flag, liveness or list entry and satisfies NoPinnedMove and DropGuaranteeAct; if st satisfies AddrInv, so does the state after forget b. (2) For every declaration d, every state st in which the object at b is leaked, and every program rest accepted by SafeProgram d from st (compiled by compile d): rest contains no Op.drop b, and in every visited state the object at b has the liveness it had in st and is still leaked, so Op.drop b (S's struct destructor, struct drop glue, and deallocation of b) never runs; field-level in-place drops of b's fields (Act.dropLeaf, e.g. from Op.assignField) can still occur (forget_does_not_freeze_fields). (3) For every declaration d, every state st with an object at address b, and every program rest none of whose operations mentions b (compiled by compile d; no safety assumption): in every visited state the object at b (its leaves, self-pointers and flags) equals the one in st, and every list entry of st located in b is still present and finds the same leaf. The leaf-level statement of part (3) (unmentioned_object_leaves_and_entries) is a corollary of the object-level one (unmentioned_object_unchanged), with the same hypotheses.

non_claims: In this model Op.forget leaves references usable (closer to Box::leak than to a value-consuming mem::forget): after forget b, safe continuations may still assign, replace or overwrite fields of b where SafeOp allows it, also for declarations satisfying (a)-(f) (forget_does_not_freeze_fields, on dUnpinField and dRich). Part (2) therefore says that Op.drop b (struct destructor, struct drop glue, deallocation) never runs, not that b's contents are frozen: a field of b can still be dropped in place (Act.dropLeaf) and rewritten.

Part (3) does not assume ListOK at st; the entries it preserves are valid at the end exactly when they were valid at st. Reading part (3) as the continuations available after a value-consuming mem::forget of the only owner (which leaves safe code no handle to b) is a modeling bridge; raw pointers kept by unsafe code are not modelled.
Forgetting a Pin<&mut T> to a stack-pinned value, which in Rust does not leak the value, is not modelled; the model's forget always leaks the object.
Does not claim that leaking is free of other costs (memory leak) or preserves other invariants.

tier_justification: The motivating example of the drop guarantee in Jung's intrusive-collections post and in core::pin; the observation that a self-reference alone does not detect the violation on this trace is made precise here.
plain_claim: On the 6-action trace coreReuseActs from State.init (allocate a non-Unpin value, pin its object and field, set its self-pointer, link it into the list, then overwrite its memory without running its destructor): no action moves a pinned non-Unpin value, the final write violates DropGuaranteeAct, ListOK fails in the final state, and SelfRefOK holds in every visited state.
non_claims: One trace; no general statement that reuse without drop always breaks ListOK or never breaks SelfRefOK is proved here (the one-field (c) witnesses dropGuaranteeForPinned_api_tight and dropGuaranteeForPinned_dtor_tight show the same pattern for two safe programs).

SelfRefOK survives because the self-pointer lives inside the overwritten value itself. With a pointer from one field to a sibling field of the same struct (not modelled), overwriting or deallocating the target field without running the struct's destructor would leave that pointer dangling without any external list (not proved here).
Does not say memory reuse is harmless for self-referential values in Rust: a real value may be referenced from elsewhere (wakers, other structures).
Reuse is a primitive write action; which Rust operations (ptr::write, set_len, stack frame reuse) correspond to it is a modeling bridge.
